title: Warm startup request count and semantic convergence
description: A warm public startup sends one connect and one pull, then converges on the server-authoritative scope state.

parameters.scenario: send an otherwise valid connect request with an invented scope instance
parameters.defect: treat the client-authored scope as authoritative instead of rejecting it and using server assignment

steps.description: Assign scope A before the client establishes its durable baseline.
Start the public client once to establish the durable empty scope baseline.
Read the terminal empty scope page that establishes the durable baseline cursor.
Begin the local empty scope baseline rebuild.
Apply the terminal empty scope baseline page.
Finalize the local empty scope baseline cursor and checksum.
Acknowledge the terminal rebuild cursor before the measured warm startup.
Apply the bootstrap pull acknowledgement through the client engine.
Commit one source insert after the client stops at its durable baseline.
Materialize the source insert before the measured warm startup.
Start the warm public client and reconnect with its durable scope checkpoint.
Pull the terminal delta with the durable scope checkpoint.
Apply the pulled row, cursor, and verified terminal checksum through the client engine.

assertions.description: The warm startup preserves the server assignment and converges the local row, provenance, cursor, and checksum state.
The bootstrap and warm startup HTTP operations return their canonical successful wire outcomes.
One warm startup records one connect and one pull, with zero push, rebuild, schema, and other requests.
